title: Own Rent Control Act, Limited to Municipal Areas
text: Kerala has not adopted the central Model Tenancy Act, 2021. Tenancies of buildings within municipal or corporation limits are governed by the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965; buildings in panchayat (rural) areas fall outside the Act and are instead governed by the general law of contract and the Transfer of Property Act, 1882.
source: Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965

title: No Statutory Cap on Advance/Deposit
text: The Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965 does not impose a fixed statutory ceiling on the advance or security deposit a landlord may collect. Deposit amounts in Kerala leases are therefore largely a matter of contract between the parties, subject to the Act's general bar on landlords charging an 'unconscionable' rent.
source: Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965 - no statutory deposit cap identified; based on targeted section review rather than an exhaustive read of the full Act, moderate confidence

title: Restricted Grounds for Eviction
text: A landlord may recover possession from a tenant under the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965 only through the Rent Control Court and only on specified grounds, including non-payment of rent within fifteen days of the due date, bona fide personal need for occupation by the landlord or a dependent family member, unauthorised subletting or transfer, material and permanent damage to the building, the tenant already possessing another suitable building, genuine need for reconstruction, or continuous non-occupation by the tenant for six months without reasonable cause. Eviction outside these grounds is not permitted for tenancies the Act covers.
source: Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965, Section 11(2)-(4)

title: Landlord Repair Duty With Tenant Self-Help Remedy
text: Notwithstanding any contract to the contrary, the landlord is bound to attend to periodical maintenance and necessary repairs of a tenanted building. If the landlord fails to do so within a reasonable time after the tenant gives notice, the Accommodation Controller may allow the tenant to carry out the repairs and deduct the cost, plus 6% annual interest, from the rent payable.
source: Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965, Section 17

title: No Cutting Off Essential Amenities
text: A landlord may not, without just or sufficient cause, cut off or withhold any amenity enjoyed by the tenant, such as water, electricity, or passage access. A tenant subjected to such a cutoff can seek an immediate interim restoration order from the Accommodation Controller - even without prior notice to the landlord - if the cutoff appears aimed at forcing eviction or a rent increase.
source: Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965, Section 13
